nonLabourLines.description: Stripe integration fees / third-party payment sandbox costs
Infrastructure (staging environment, CI runners) setup costs

assumptions: The supplied rate card is a PLACEHOLDER: a single 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour with only 1 FTE available. All costs below are indicative only and MUST be revisited once real team members are assigned roles (e.g. Frontend, Backend, QA, DevOps) and given their own hourly rates — a single generalist rate materially understates cost for specialist work like the Oracle migration or Stripe integration.

No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet, so this estimate is built purely from story points translated into effort hours and the placeholder rate — it is not calibrated against real velocity or cost history.

Story points were converted to engineering hours using an approximate 5 hours per point baseline (typical for small/well-understood tasks), scaled up for tasks with inherent complexity or risk (legacy migration, payment integration, multi-currency, RBAC) to 7-8 hours per point to reflect integration, testing and edge-case overhead.

Total estimated effort across the 24 backlog items is ~2,320 hours. With only 1 FTE available on the placeholder rate card (working ~1,700-1,880 productive hours/year), this backlog represents well over a full year of solo effort — the team is staffed far too thinly for this scope. This MUST be flagged to the client/PM: either headcount needs to increase, timeline needs to extend past 12 months, or scope needs to be cut.
Non-labour costs are rough placeholders for Stripe fees/sandbox, Oracle migration tooling, and CI/staging infrastructure — actual vendor quotes have not been obtained.

Scenario spread (Optimistic -12%, Most Likely baseline, Pessimistic +27%) reflects typical uncertainty for a backlog with a large, risky data migration (PW-8) and a payment integration (PW-7), both of which are common sources of overrun.
Priority breakdown costs are derived pro-rata from each task's estimated hours at the 75 USD/hour placeholder rate, then summed by priority tag.
Points-to-hours mapping assumed: Urgent/High-risk complex items (PW-4, PW-7, PW-8, PW-9, PW-14) weighted at ~7-8 hrs/point; all other items at ~5 hrs/point.
input.reasoning: Effort was derived by converting each backlog item's story points into hours using a baseline of ~5 hours/point for straightforward items, increased to 7-8 hours/point for items carrying higher technical risk or integration complexity (RBAC, payment integration, legacy data migration, GDPR workflows, multi-currency). Summing across all 24 items gives ~2,320 hours of total engineering effort. Since the rate card provided is a placeholder with a single generic 'Team member' role at 75 USD/hour, all effort was booked to that one role — cost = hours x 75 for every line, verified via check_estimate. Non-labour costs were added for the three items with clear external cost exposure: Stripe integration/sandbox fees, Oracle migration tooling, and CI/staging infrastructure setup. Three scenarios were produced around the baseline (Most Likely = sum of line items exactly, at 177,500 USD): an Optimistic case assuming some efficiency gains reduce the estimate by ~12%, and a Pessimistic case reflecting the very real risk of overruns on the legacy migration and payment integration, adding ~27%. Given only 1 FTE is available against ~2,320 hours of backlog, this estimate should be read as a total-cost figure rather than a deliverable timeline — the client needs to add headcount or accept a materially longer delivery schedule, or cut scope, which is addressed in the reduction recommendations.

reductions.description: Descope PW-18 (Admin back-office for support staff), PW-19 (Usage analytics and reporting), PW-23 (Contract tests against helpdesk API) and PW-24 (Decommission legacy portal) — all tagged Low priority — from this phase and move to a later release.
reductions.effect: Removes ~340 hours of low-priority backlog scope from the initial delivery; can be picked up in a follow-on phase once core portal is live.

reductions.description: Defer PW-14 (Multi-currency support) until after initial launch — most customers can likely be served in a single settlement currency at go-live, with multi-currency added once real demand is confirmed.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~100 hours of medium-priority scope; re-adds risk of rework if multi-currency is needed sooner, but avoids speculative investment.

reductions.description: Reduce scope of PW-8 (Legacy data migration) to a phased migration (migrate active accounts first, archive/cold-migrate the remainder later) rather than a single big-bang migration of all 400k records and 2M invoice lines.
reductions.effect: Cuts ~200 hours from the highest-risk, highest-effort item by narrowing the first-pass migration scope; remaining data migrated in a lower-priority follow-up.

reductions.description: Defer PW-15 (Accessibility pass to WCAG 2.2 AA) to immediately after launch rather than in the initial build, unless a compliance deadline forces it into scope now.
reductions.effect: Removes ~80 hours from the initial phase; carries legal/compliance risk if accessibility is a hard requirement, so should only be deferred with client sign-off.

reductions.description: Reduce non-labour spend by using free-tier/sandbox Stripe testing and open-source CI runners instead of paid infrastructure during the build phase, deferring paid tiers to closer to go-live.
reductions.effect: Cuts non-labour costs from 3,500 to ~2,500 during the initial build; paid tiers re-added before production launch.
